title: Hypothesis Testing for Variance and Standard Deviation

back: To test a claim about a population variance $\sigma^2$ or standard deviation $\sigma$.
The test statistic follows a chi‑square distribution with $d.f. = n-1$.
cards.front: When is a [[kw:chi‑square test]] used in hypothesis testing?

back: $s^2$ is the sample variance, $\sigma^2_0$ is the hypothesized variance from $H_0$.
If testing a standard deviation, square both $s$ and $\sigma_0$ first.
cards.front: Give the formula for the [[kw:chi‑square test statistic]] for a variance.
How do you find the critical value for a [[kw:right‑tailed]] chi‑square test?
back: Use the chi‑square table with $d.f. = n-1$ and area $\alpha$ in the right tail.
The area to the left of the critical value is $\alpha$, so the area to the right is $1-\alpha$.
cards.front: How do you find the critical value for a [[kw:left‑tailed]] chi‑square test?

back: Two critical values: $\chi^2_L$ (area to left = $\alpha/2$) and $\chi^2_R$ (area to right = $\alpha/2$).
[[imp:They are not opposites]] because the chi‑square distribution is skewed.
cards.front: How do you find the critical values for a [[kw:two‑tailed]] chi‑square test?
A dairy company claims $\sigma^2 \le 0.25$. A sample of 41 containers has $s^2 = 0.27$. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ (normal population).
back: $43.2 < 55.758$ → [[imp:fail to reject $H_0$]]. Not enough evidence to reject the claim.
$14.816 < 15.659$ → [[imp:reject $H_0$]]. Enough evidence to support the claim.
cards.front: A company claims $\sigma < 1.4$ minutes for call transfers. A sample of 25 calls has $s=1.1$ min. Test at $\alpha=0.10$ (normal).

back: Right‑tailed P‑value = area to the right of the test statistic.
cards.front: Find the P‑value for a right‑tailed chi‑square test with $\chi^2 = 43.2$ and $d.f. = 40$.

back: Left‑tailed P‑value = area to the left of the test statistic.
cards.front: Find the P‑value for a left‑tailed chi‑square test with $\chi^2 = 14.816$ and $d.f. = 24$.

back: Because the distribution is skewed, you find the left‑tail and right‑tail areas, then double the [[imp:smaller]] of the two.
Left area = `=CHISQ.DIST(χ², d.f., TRUE)`. Right area = `=CHISQ.DIST.RT(χ², d.f.)`.
cards.front: How do you find the two‑tailed P‑value for a chi‑square test?

back: The chi‑square test is [[imp:not robust]] to departures from normality.
If the population is skewed, the actual Type I error rate can be very different from $\alpha$.
Always check for approximate normality before using this test.
cards.front: Why is the normality assumption critical for a chi‑square test of a variance?

back: $\chi^2 = \frac{14 \times 21.8}{15.9} \approx 19.195$. Not in rejection region → [[imp:fail to reject $H_0$]].
cards.front: A manufacturer claims $\sigma^2 = 15.9$. A sample of 15 has $s^2 = 21.8$. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ (normal).
A weather service claims $\sigma \le 25$ fatalities per year. A sample of 28 years has $s = 31$. Test at $\alpha=0.10$ (normal).
back: $41.53 > 36.741$ → [[imp:reject $H_0$]]. Enough evidence to reject the claim.

cards.front: What are the degrees of freedom for a chi‑square test on a sample of size $n$?
back: Same as for a t‑test and confidence interval for variance.

back: This is the cutoff; reject $H_0$ if $\chi^2 > 30.144$.
